question: Head Office of erstwhile Allahabad Bank was located at:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kolkata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Allahabad Bank was one of the oldest joint stock banks in India, founded in 1865.
 
• The head office of Allahabad Bank was located in Kolkata, West Bengal.
 
• Allahabad Bank was nationalized in 1969 by the Government of India.
 
• In April 2020, Allahabad Bank was merged with Indian Bank, and its branches now function under Indian Bank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Banking System**

 
 
• The Indian banking system consists of public sector banks, private sector banks, foreign banks, regional rural banks (RRBs), and cooperative banks.
 
• Public sector banks are those where the majority stake is held by the government.
 
• As of the latest data, there are 12 public sector banks in India after several mergers and consolidations.
 
• Private sector banks are those where the majority of the stake is held by private entities or individuals.
 
 
 
• **Nationalization of Banks**
 
 
• The first major nationalization of banks in India happened in 1969 when 14 large commercial banks were nationalized.
 
• The second phase of nationalization occurred in 1980, with six more banks being nationalized.
 
• Nationalization aimed at spreading banking infrastructure across the country and ensuring that credit is available to all sectors of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Merger of Banks**
 
 
• Bank mergers are aimed at creating larger and stronger banks that can compete globally.
 
• In 2019, the Indian government announced the merger of 10 public sector banks into four entities.
 
• The merger of Allahabad Bank with Indian Bank was part of this consolidation strategy.
 
• Such mergers help in improving operational efficiency, capital base, and customer services.
